name: Del McCoury Band
sources: style-research-extended-2 vol.2 country-train — Del McCoury Band
notes: High-lonesome traditional bluegrass at full tempo, played by a family band around a single microphone, and the entry calls it "the section's strictest realisation of the drummerless archetype". Flagship because the research rates it high-medium with lineup, instrument roles, era, awards and the single-mic technique all sourced. The section states the rule this whole wing turns on: "the train beat is an ensemble function, not a drum part" — the banjo roll carries the continuous subdivision, the mandolin chop supplies the backbeat, and the upright bass supplies the two-beat kick. This entry names each player against each job — banjo roll = subdivision, mandolin chop = backbeat "placed driven (close to the preceding bass note) for maximum drive", upright = the two-beat, fiddle floats — and states "none, ever, in the core band" for drums. So `snare.offGridMs` is −8, the earliest backbeat anywhere in this section and the direct encoding of "driven"; `kick` is a flat 2 on anchors 1 and 3 for the upright's two-beat; the hat is on quarters, not continuous, at a 0.02 fill density; and `percs` is rim and woodblock at −13 dB, the quietest percussion here. Keys are the stated B♭/A/G/D, chosen high "to sit the lead vocal at the top of its range (the high lonesome placement is a key decision, not just a timbre)", and the melody register runs 64–88 for the same reason. Harmony is "I–IV–V almost exclusively, with V7 and occasional II7 (secondary dominant)" — the II7 is authored as the degree II, with the seventh carried in `extensions`. The bass is the sourced upright idiom: root–five alternation with walking excursions, slap accents on the fast numbers, anticipated timing, so `anticipationProb` is 0.3, the highest in the wing. ⚠ The single-microphone technique has a stated generator consequence — "dynamics are created by players stepping toward and away from the mic, so model arrangement-level dynamics as instrument-level gain automation, with only one or two instruments at full level at a time" — which this schema cannot express; it is recorded here rather than encoded, and the rotating-break arrangement is the closest reachable expression of it. ⚠ INFERRED: velocity tiers, the −8 ms value itself, `percs` contents and every melody, countermelody and bassline number. ⚠ The entry states "tempo band inferred from the breakdown convention [LOW-CONF]", so `bpm.mode` 180 inside the stated 120–210 carries that flag.
